The initial check found two banned words and the final check found zero.
The file notes/report.md held two booster words.
Each booster word was rewritten to neutral language.
The final tool check confirmed zero failures.

# Background

The task requested execution of a five-step runbook on notes/report.md.
Step 1 read the target file.
Step 2 through Step 4 detected and removed banned words.

# Relevance

Removing banned vocabulary ensures compliance with controlled writing rules.
This verification protects document delivery quality.

# Information

The tool check_file executed on notes/report.md at Step 2 [P].
It reported two banned booster words: "clearly" and "robust" [P].
Therefore, Step 3 replaced "clearly" with "measurably" and "robust" with "operational" [P].
Step 4 executed check_file again and reported zero banned words [P].

Assumption log:
Assumption: Replacing the two booster words with neutral adjectives preserves the author intent. Why not measured: The material does not state preferred synonyms. Validate by: Review with the document author. If wrong: Replace with alternative approved adjectives.

Alternative considered:
Delete the booster words entirely without substituting adjectives. It loses because replacing each word directly preserves sentence grammatical structure.

# End

I recommend that we:

1. Maintain notes/report.md with the rewritten terms.
This increment keeps the compliant report in the repository.
It removes non-compliant booster words from the documentation.
Test kind: Deterministic.
Given the file notes/report.md
When check_file runs on it
Then zero banned words are reported
Cynefin domain: Clear, deduction from deterministic tool rules.

2. Add check_file to the continuous integration pipeline.
This increment configures automated pre-commit checking for markdown notes.
It adds automated prevention of banned terms in future edits.
Test kind: Deterministic.

When the continuous integration lint job runs
Then check_file reports zero banned words before merge
Cynefin domain: Clear, deduction from standard pipeline configuration.

3. Audit remaining markdown files in the repository for banned terms.
This increment scans all existing documentation using list_files and check_file.
It removes latent vocabulary violations across the repository.
Test kind: Deterministic.
Given all markdown files listed by list_files
When check_file runs across all paths
Then every file passes with zero failures
Cynefin domain: Clear, deduction from systematic execution across repository paths.
